LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_Easy_Desc: Lower tiers, softer mood swings. Forgiving food variety.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_Hardcore_Desc: Raised tiers, full mood weight. For experienced colonies.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_Easy_Tooltip: Sets tier memory 7–27 meals, palate 2–36%, mood range -8/+12 (soft penalties, full rewards), meal bonus 0/10/20/30/40%, slave/prisoner 50%/40%. Most forgiving; recommended for new players or low-food colonies.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_Default_Tooltip: Sets tier memory 9–34 meals, palate 4–48%, mood range -12/+12, meal bonus 0/5/12/20/30%, slave/prisoner 65%/50%. The mod's balanced baseline.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_Hardcore_Tooltip: Recommended for experienced players. Sets tier memory 11–40 meals, palate 6–50%, mood range -14/+12 (harsher penalties), meal bonus 0/3/8/14/22%, slave/prisoner 80%/65%. High-expectation pawns (Noble) will need 50+ unique ingredients stockpiled or they will complain persistently.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Preset_CustomDesc: Individual tuning — no preset matches the current settings.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Scoring_Body: Each meal is scored from 0% to 100% by how many of its ingredients are absent from the pawn's last 6 meals. Fully-fresh ingredients score 100%; full repeats score 0%. A meal whose recipe type has not appeared in the pawn's full memory queue earns an extra bonus on top: +0 for 1-slot (simple), +5% for 2-slot (fine / lavish), and up to +30% for modded 5-slot recipes. Each pawn's palate threshold is set by their expectation tier (Noble has the highest bar). Variety mood = average(per-meal effective) × memory multiplier, capped at 100%.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_NonControlledPawnsLabel: Non controlled pawns also have variety need:
LanguageData.VM_Settings_NonControlledPawnsTooltip: Enables food-variety tracking for non-colonist pawns (guests, visitors, mechanoids' handlers, etc.). Off by default means only your controlled colonists care about variety.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_FoodDrugsOnceLabel: Foods that are also drugs are stored in memory just once:
LanguageData.VM_Settings_FoodDrugsOnceTooltip: Foods that also serve as drugs are stored in memory only once. This allows for a scheduled intake of these substances without diminishing variety, while still enjoying the benefits of having them considered as variety if the pawns likes them as food.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PreferVarietyTooltip: Cooks rotate ingredients across meals and mix distinct ThingDefs within a single meal. Mixing only applies to bills with 'Allow mixing ingredients' enabled — bills without mixing still get variety-weighted sort order but remain single-ingredient per slot.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PreferSpoilingTooltip: Cooks prioritize ingredients that are closer to spoiling, reducing food waste. Doesn't affect variety scoring — only ingredient selection order when multiple stacks are eligible.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_StackByIngredientsTooltip: When enabled, cooked meals with different ingredient sets do NOT stack together in storage — each distinct ingredient combo keeps its own stack. Required for the per-meal variety score to work correctly (otherwise all meals of a type merge into one bag and ingredient history is lost). Disable only if you want vanilla stacking behavior.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_NumIngredientsTooltip: Maximum distinct ingredient ThingDefs the cook will stuff into a single produced meal when 'Cooks use different ingredients' is on. Higher values = more variety per plate but harder pantry management. Vanilla caps at 3; setting this lower throttles the mod's mixing behavior.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_CookingMemoryDepthTooltip: How many recent meals each cook remembers when picking ingredients for the next one. Higher = wider rotation (cook avoids repeating ingredients across more past meals). Purely a cooking-AI knob — does NOT affect the pawn-side variety mood window.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_ExpectationExplanation: Each tier has two independently-tunable knobs: Memory (how many past meals that pawn averages into mood) and Palate (how fresh a meal needs to be before it registers). Higher memory = more inertia. Higher palate = harder to satisfy, but also means top-quality meals push mood higher. Defaults: Noble remembers 34 meals with palate 48%; Extremely Low remembers 9 with palate 4%.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Tier_MemoryTooltip: Number of past meals this tier averages into variety mood. Higher values smooth the mood score — a single bad meal has less impact — but also slow recovery when variety is restored. Typical range: 9 (Extremely Low) to 34 (Noble).
LanguageData.VM_Settings_Tier_PalateTooltip: How fresh a meal needs to be, as a percentage, before it counts meaningfully toward mood. Meals below this threshold contribute only 25% of their raw ingredient-fresh score; meals above it get full credit proportional to how far above. 0% = any variety counts; 50% = only genuinely fresh meals matter (max). Typical range: 4% (Extremely Low) to 48% (Noble).
LanguageData.VM_Settings_MealBonus_Body: A meal whose recipe type hasn't been seen in the pawn's memory queue gets an additive variety bonus on top of its ingredient-fresh score. The bonus scales with recipe complexity (number of ingredient slots in the recipe definition, NOT the stuffed ingredient count of the produced meal). Simple meals (1 slot) get nothing by default; vanilla fine/lavish (2 slots) earn a small +5%; modded 3+ slot recipes escalate. Set any slot to 0 to disable its bonus.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_LowExpectationFloorTooltip: Hard floor on expected variety count after all tier / slave / prisoner / gourmand modifiers. Keeps tribal / Naked Brutality starts from dropping to 1–2 and trivializing early-game food variety. Raise to make the early game harder; lower to give low-expectation colonies an easier ride.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_SlaveExpectedVarietyLabel: Slave expected variety (% of tier, default 65%):
LanguageData.VM_Settings_SlaveExpectedVarietyTooltip: Percentage applied to the slave's tier value. Scales both expected-variety count AND palate threshold. 100% = same as a free pawn of the same tier; 50% = half as picky.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PrisonerExpectedVarietyLabel: Prisoner expected variety (% of tier, default 50%):
LanguageData.VM_Settings_PrisonerExpectedVarietyToolt: Percentage applied to the prisoner's tier value. Scales both expected-variety count AND palate threshold. 100% = same as a free pawn of the same tier; 50% = half as picky.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_MoodMaxNegTooltip: The worst-case mood penalty the variety thought can produce at the most-barren stage. Stages scale linearly toward 0 at the "average menu" stage. Set 0 to disable all negative variety mood. Vanilla-equivalent default is -12. Gourmand trait doubles this on top.
LanguageData.VM_Settings_MoodMaxPosTooltip: The best-case mood bonus the variety thought can produce at the most-varied stage. Stages scale linearly toward 0 at the "average menu" stage. Set 0 to disable all positive variety mood. Vanilla-equivalent default is +12. Gourmand trait doubles this on top.
